title: Gas pressure and standard conditions
log: 2026-11-01T08:04:32Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: None of the bank points defines gas pressure as force per area or introduces standard laboratory conditions; the closest, molar volume, only uses 25°C and 100 kPa as conditions for a calculation, so a new point is needed.

draft.title: Gas pressure and standard conditions
card: Pressure is force divided by the area it acts on. Gas pressure comes from particles hitting the walls of their container.
The unit of pressure is the pascal (Pa). One kilopascal (kPa) is 1000 Pa.
More collisions or harder collisions on the same area mean a higher pressure. Squeezing the same gas into a smaller container raises its pressure.
Standard laboratory conditions (SLC) are a temperature of 25 °C and a pressure of 100 kPa. Using the same conditions lets chemists compare gases fairly.
draft.remember: Pressure is force per area. Standard laboratory conditions are 25 °C and 100 kPa.

a.q: A force of 600 N acts on an area of 2 m². What is the pressure?
a.why: Pressure = force ÷ area = 600 ÷ 2 = 300 Pa. Multiplying instead of dividing gives 1200 Pa, which is the tempting mistake.
a.clue: Divide the force by the area.

b.q: Priya collects a gas in her school lab at 25 °C and 100 kPa. What can she say about these conditions?
opts: They are only found at sea level
They give a pressure of 100 Pa
b.why: A temperature of 25 °C and a pressure of 100 kPa are the standard laboratory conditions. The pressure is 100 kPa, which is 100 000 Pa, not 100 Pa.
b.clue: Compare her numbers with the card.
